snippet.title: Pixygarden [ピクシーガーデン] Game Sample - Playstation
snippet.description:
You folks enjoying this string of Japan-only curiosities? If so, that's fantastic! If not, then that's cool too -- you'll be pleased to know that we're near the end of this run. This is a title I've wanted to do for a long time but as there was little info at the time and it has a steep initial learning curve, I put it on hold... but I'm stubborn, ya know? I'd like to present... Pixygarden!

What is Pixygarden? Released for the Playstation in late 1999 by Escot and Imageworks, it is actually the third incarnation, or a remake of a remake, of a planet sim game that was released prior for Japanese Windows 95 in 1998 ("Pixygarden Adavanced: Terre promise") and PC-98 in 1995 ("Pixygarden: A Fairy Legend"). The PS game has streamlined the concepts of the PC-98/Win95 game, had a promotional push by enlisting Moe Katagiri (who voices the main heroine, Neredy/Nereid, and sings the song "Tanpopo") and hiring the now-popular illustrator, CHOCO, (also known as "Chocolate Shop", he has done designs for "CHAOS; HEAD", "Infinite Stratos", the "Xenosaga" series, etc.) to update the fairy designs, and came packaged as a two disc set for a limited time which included art, interviews, and a collectible card holder (one of five). All iterations of the game are seen as obscure even within the Japanese community, but are noted for their complexity, relaxing nature and beautiful art.

What's fascinating is that the main story is outlined in the PC-98 version in English, but to summarize: The player is the leader of an Intergalactic Frontier Team known only as the "Miracle Man", who has figured out a way to colonize other planets by turning their atmospheres into those similar to the Earth, but what people don't know is that he's been capable of doing this due to the tale of an old woman he met in the woods while growing up. By believing in the supernatural and manipulating the power of fairies by appealing to their sensibilities, he has bridged the gap between the human world and fairy world, known as "Global", in an effort to save mankind's future. By placing the appropriate objects on a planet's surface, he can gain the favor of the four major elements: Earth, Water, Wind and Fire. The player has a certain number of days to manipulate a planet's landscape before the immigrant ship colonies arrive to inhabit them. The PS game's plot is modified a bit to include these planets within what the game calls the "Hectas Star System" with an A.I. companion named Neredy (sometimes seen as Nereid) who guides the player and explains the planet's different circumstances.

It should go without saying, but this is a rather pretty 2D (or perhaps 2.5D) PS game, even if the graphical assets are fairly limited; the sprites have a good bit of detail and animation, the standard art is nice and the game also uses high-res art during galleries or in the "Pixy Tree". There are six planets or "stages" (one easy, four normal, one hard), but they don't all have unique backdrops unfortunately... the objects you can use on some are a bit different and the events are different though. The music is also nice and relaxing with a few tracks to listen to, which is good because you'll be hearing them a lot. The game doesn't have much voice acting, but what is present is good.

The real kicker here is the gameplay. It's simple on the surface: your goal is to utilize pixies, gardens, modus, transfer modules, thermo adjustment, music and points to increase elemental attributes within a planet to high enough levels where it can sustain human life... okay, maybe it's not so simple. So, objects with different spirit powers can be placed in four quadrants where transfer modules will absorb their essence. From there, pixies wander around aimlessly or can be placed in these quadrants and take the absorbed energy from the transfer modules. After that, pixies can evolve into various forms based on their makeup and absorb elements at a higher rate as well as "generate modus" based on their mood or "engage the planet". When engaging the planet, Evolved Pixies can take one of four points and distribute the elements they took from the transfer module to help develop the planet, or use a modus as a stand-in (they don't have much, but they buy time while your Pixy stays in the garden and gains elements to evolve even further as the planet drains them). 

The basic flow is: Select Garden (helps cultivate Pixies) --} Place Objects --} Move Pixies --} Evolve Pixies --} Get Modus --} Move a Pixy or Modus to Points --} Repeat. On top of this, you can adjust the temperature of the planet or change the background music to aid in the evolution of certain types of Pixies (EX: Extreme heat improves fire elements, the music track "Windmill" improves Wind, etc.) and certain objects, evolutions and in-game days can determine what events and hidden objects you encounter. While it's more of an idle sim than anything, there is quite a bit buried within for those patient enough to dig it out.
